title: Etale descent of Tor amplitude and local finite Tor dimension
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\epsilon_X:(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})\to(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X)$ the canonical morphism of ringed sites, with tensor module pullback $\epsilon_X^*$ [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be arbitrary. Use unbounded derived categories of sheaves of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$ for the derived tensor product, computed by a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex] and the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. An object $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, for integers $a\le b$, if $H^j(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)=0$ for every structure-module sheaf $F$ and every $j\notin[a,b]$. It has finite Tor dimension if such an interval exists; it locally has finite Tor dimension if locally on every site object some such interval exists, allowed to depend on the covering member. For every $a\le b$, $E$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and only if $\epsilon_X^*E$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. In addition, $E$ locally has finite Tor dimension in the Zariski topology if and only if $\epsilon_X^*E$ locally has finite Tor dimension in the small etale topology. No quasi-coherence or global boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], $\epsilon_X^*$ is exact and faithful on ALL structure-module sheaves, without quasi-coherence. Its termwise functor therefore represents its derived functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to obtain $H^j(\epsilon_X^*C)\simeq\epsilon_X^*H^j(C)$ for every complex $C$. Exactness identifies $L\epsilon_X^*$ with this termwise functor, so [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] supplies, in the unbounded derived category, $\epsilon_X^*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)\simeq\epsilon_X^*E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_X^*F$. These statements apply to any scheme in place of $X$.

source.place: Tag 08HF, lemma-descend-tor-amplitude, converse proof; Tag 08H8, lemma-epsilon-flat; tensor comparison: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text: Suppose $E$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-sp-ringed-site-tor-flat-model] on the Zariski ringed site to represent $E$ by a flat-term complex $P$ zero outside $[a,b]$. This is a bounded-above complex on the ringed space $(X,\mathcal O_X)$, so [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat] makes it K-flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] to $P$: $\epsilon_X^*P$ has flat terms, and its terms still vanish outside $[a,b]$. By exact-functor localization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and Step 1 it represents $\epsilon_X^*E$. The reverse implication in [lem-sp-ringed-site-tor-flat-model], now on the small etale site, proves the required Tor interval against EVERY etale structure-module sheaf, including those not pulled back from the Zariski site.

source.place: Tag 08H5, lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback, proof using Tag 08G1, lemma-tor-amplitude; K-flat pullback: Tag 0G7E; Zariski bounded-flat input: cohomology.tex Tag 06YD

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $\epsilon_X^*E$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. For any Zariski structure-module sheaf $F$, the tensor comparison of Step 1 identifies $\epsilon_X^*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)$ with $\epsilon_X^*E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_X^*F$, whose $j$th cohomology is zero for $j\notin[a,b]$. The exact-functor cohomology isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies this zero sheaf with $\epsilon_X^*H^j(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)$. Faithfulness in [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] forces $H^j(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)=0$: if its pullback is zero, its identity pulls back to zero, hence is zero. Since $F$ was arbitrary, $E$ has the same Tor interval.

Taking the existential quantifier over the same integers $a\le b$ in Steps 2 and 3 proves that $E$ has finite Tor dimension if and only if $\epsilon_X^*E$ does. This does not assert that either object is globally bounded for an arbitrary input; boundedness is a consequence only when such an interval exists.

source.place: Tag 08HF, lemma-descend-tor-amplitude, assertion (2); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude

proof.text: For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, write $r_U$ for restriction to the etale object $U$. The site equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] identifies $(X_{\mathrm{et}})/U$ with $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. It identifies the structure rings as well, since both assign $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ to an etale $V\to U$; hence it identifies module sheaves and complexes with these same sectionwise operations. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] the inverse image $j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ along the etale map $j$ is restriction along $U_{\mathrm{et}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$; it carries $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ to $\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}$ with identity ring map, so the tensor pullback $j_{\mathrm{et}}^*=\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}}j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}(-)$ is $r_U$ under this identification. For Zariski modules, $j^*$ is ordinary restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction]. Apply [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square] with $a=j$ to get $\epsilon_U^*j^*\simeq r_U\epsilon_X^*$. Both restrictions are exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and both epsilon pullbacks are exact by Step 1. Consequently the same comparison applied termwise gives $\epsilon_U^*(E|_U)\simeq(\epsilon_X^*E)|_U$ in the unbounded derived category, using [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

source.place: Tag 03FH, remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites (2), specialized to an open immersion; localization: sites.tex Tag 00XZ and sites-modules.tex Tag 04IX

proof.text: Assume $E$ locally has finite Tor dimension in the Zariski topology. There is an open covering $\{U_i\}$ of $X$ on which $E|_{U_i}$ has some interval $[a_i,b_i]$. Steps 2 and 5 give that same interval for $(\epsilon_X^*E)|_{U_i}$. For any etale object $V\to X$, the base changes $V\times_XU_i\to V$ form an etale covering by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Restrict the interval on $U_i$ to $V\times_XU_i$ using [lem-sf-site-tor-interval-restriction]; the successive restrictions agree by the sectionwise relocalization formula in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Thus every etale object has a covering on which the restricted complex has finite Tor dimension, precisely the local definition in the statement.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude (3); Tag 08H5, lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback, applied to site localization

proof.text: Now suppose $\epsilon_X^*E$ locally has finite Tor dimension. Fix a NONEMPTY affine open $U\subseteq X$. By Step 5 and the local definition, there is an etale covering $\{v_i:V_i\to U\}$ on which the restriction of $\epsilon_U^*(E|_U)$ has intervals $[a_i,b_i]$. Every image $v_i(V_i)$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. These images cover $U$ by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Since an affine scheme is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], the definition [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] supplies finitely many indices $i_1,\ldots,i_n$ whose images cover $U$, with $n\ge1$. Put $a=\min_k a_{i_k}$ and $b=\max_k b_{i_k}$. Then $a\le b$ and every selected local interval is contained in $[a,b]$. This interval may depend on $U$, which is all local finite Tor dimension requires.

source.place: Tag 08HF, lemma-descend-tor-amplitude, local application of (1); open images: morphisms.tex Tag 03WT; finite subcover: algebra.tex Tag 00E8 and topology.tex Tag 005A

proof.text:
Set $K=\epsilon_U^*(E|_U)$ and let $F$ be ANY degree-zero etale structure-module sheaf on $U$. Restriction $r_k$ to $V_{i_k}$ is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] for the etale map $V_{i_k}\to U$, $r_k$ is the inverse image of the induced morphism of small etale topoi; its ring map is the identity on the restricted structure ring [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], so its tensor and derived pullbacks are this restriction. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology],
$$r_kH^j(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)\simeq H^j(K|_{V_{i_k}}\otimes^{\mathbf L}F|_{V_{i_k}})=0\quad(j\notin[a,b]).$$
These vanishings imply $H^j(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)=0$: for any etale $W\to U$, the family $W\times_UV_{i_k}\to W$ covers, and every section restricts to zero on its members, hence is zero by the separatedness axiom of a sheaf. As $F$ was arbitrary, $K$ has Tor interval $[a,b]$. Step 3 applied to the scheme $U$ gives this interval for $E|_U$. The empty affine open has only zero sheaves and may use $[0,0]$. The affine opens contained in any open $W\subseteq X$ cover $W$, so $E$ locally has finite Tor dimension on the Zariski site. No compactness of $X$ or quasi-coherence of $E,F$ was used.
